title: Introduce synthetic latent perturbation smokecheck CI hook
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a CI smokecheck that validates prompt-set robustness under controlled synthetic perturbations (semantic/latent). Introduces a new PRS metric and Actions artifact summarizer. Backwards-compatible; opt-in by default.
files_changed_summary: Added synthetic_perturber module, CI hook entrypoint, PRS metric implementation, small test-suite, docs example, and action/workflow summary HTML; modified anchor snapshot registry to accept perturbation baselines.
commit_summary: 3 commits: (1) add synthetic perturbation generator and PRS metric; (2) wire CI hook + Actions artifact; (3) deterministic seeding + tests and docs
description:
Summary: Adds a lightweight CI smokecheck that probes prompt-set stability by applying small synthetic perturbations in the latent/embedding space and measuring end-to-end output fidelity. Motivation: many regressions manifest only under small semantic perturbations (paraphrases, tokenisation shifts, embedding noise). Current stability checks focus on exact-match or gold-similarity; this PR creates a reproducible adversarial-style probe to surface fragility early in CI.

Design and behavior: The feature introduces a synthetic_latent_perturber component and a smokehook (ci/smoke_perturbation_check) that runs on pull requests. The perturber supports two strategies: (A) gaussian latent noise applied to embeddings (configurable sigma per strength level), and (B) paraphrase-driven surface perturbations using a small local paraphrase model or cached paraphrase lexicon. The hook runs a small sample of anchor prompt examples across three perturbation strengths: light/medium/heavy. For each run it computes the Perturbation Robustness Score (PRS), a composite metric that combines semantic similarity (embedding cosine) and task-specific fidelity (task-dependent scorer or answer overlap when applicable). PRS is normalized [0,100]. The hook compares PRS against the baseline anchor snapshot (stored under eval-harness/anchors/) and flags CI failure if either: (1) absolute PRS falls below baseline_threshold (default 70) OR (2) PRS delta drops more than allowed_delta (default 6 points) on light/medium checks. Heavy strength is informative only (does not gate by default).

CI integration: The smokehook is wired to GitHub Actions and emits an artifacts JSON plus an HTML summary visible in the workflow run. The hook is opt-in via .github/eval-hooks.yml and defaults to run on PRs that touch eval-related paths or when label "eval-smoke" is present. Results are uploaded to Actions artifacts and create a short comment on the PR summary with PRS numbers. The hook is intentionally sample-limited (default 25 prompts) to keep runtime < 2 minutes on hosted runners.

Determinism and reproducibility: Early review flagged nondeterminism from the paraphrase generator. Changes made in this PR address that: paraphrase generation is seeded, and paraphrase outputs are cached per-anchor (with an offline cache builder script). The latent noise path uses a fixed RNG seed pathable from the ci config. The smokehook supports a --replay mode that runs against historical anchor snapshots for backfills.

Failure modes and mitigations: We do not rely solely on paraphrase generators for gating; the PRS composite blends embedding similarity and task fidelity to avoid false positives. The default thresholds are conservative and intended to catch large regressions without blocking noisy model churn. Operators can tune thresholds per prompt-set.

Developer experience: Added a CLI wrapper (eval-hook run-perturb) and an example in docs/eval_harness/perturbation_smoke.md showing how to run locally against an anchor. Also added a small unit/integration test-suite that runs in CI.

Checklist: - [x] synthetic_perturber implementation (latent & paraphrase paths) - [x] PRS metric and baseline snapshot handling - [x] CI hook + Actions artifact + PR comment summarizer - [x] deterministic seeding & caching - [x] tests and sample fixtures - [x] docs and runbook snippet

Changed files (high-level): - eval_harness/perturb/synthetic_perturber.py (new) - eval_harness/metrics/perturbation_prs.py (new) - ci/hooks/smoke_perturbation_check.py (new) - .github/workflows/perturb_smoke.yml (new) - docs/eval_harness/perturbation_smoke.md (new) - eval_harness/anchors/README.md (updated to document perturb baselines) - tests/test_perturb_smoke.py (new) - tests/fixtures/anchors/perturb/ (new samples)

Commits: 1) "perturb: add synthetic_latent_perturber and PRS metric" 2) "ci: add smoke_perturbation_check hook and Actions artifact" 3) "tests/docs: add deterministic seeding, caches, tests, docs"

Review conversation (abridged): - Ravi Patel: "Nice concept. Two asks: (a) ensure paraphrase generator cache size is bounded, (b) show example PR comment content in the docs." - Maya Chen (author): "(a) added cache eviction policy and store size cap, (b) included sample comment payload in docs." - Ana Gómez: "We should avoid gating on heavy perturbations; otherwise good." - Maya Chen: "Heavy strength is informational only by default; added explicit config flag to promote if teams want stricter checks." - Connor Lee (approval): "Verified deterministic runs locally and smoke workflow output; lgtm pending CI."

CI runs: First Actions run (2025-07-15) failed: nondeterministic paraphrase selection caused one sample to generate different paraphrase across runs leading to a PRS delta > allowed_delta. Fix: added deterministic seed + cache builder. Rerun (2025-07-17) passed all gating checks on main test fixtures. Final CI pass (2025-07-20) prior to merge.

Why this is different: Existing eval gates focus on response-level deltas or cohort-driven regressions; this PR explicitly probes small semantic perturbations in latent space to catch fragility that would otherwise be quiet on clean inputs. It intentionally blends lightweight runtime with a conservative gating policy so it can run in PR CI without significant cost.

Operational notes and next steps: - Suggested default thresholds and sample sizes are in docs; platform teams can enable per-repo stricter settings. - We plan an optional Canary expansion which will run the full prompt-set (non-sampled) nightly for high-sensitivity workloads. - Follow-up: add a streaming-friendly runner for dedicated CI workers so larger sample sizes can be used without impacting PR latency.

Merged-by: Connor Lee (squash).
notes: Opt-in, low-runtime PR smokecheck. PRS is experimental; we tracked conservative default thresholds and added docs to ease adoption. Deterministic paraphrase caching was the main stabilization change after initial CI failure.
